title: Life on the Space Station
subtitle: 考点：太空生活 / weightless, fall asleep, on board
passage: Astronauts on the International Space Station live and work in a very different world. There is almost no gravity there, so everything seems weightless. Food, pens and even water float in the air, and astronauts must tie their tools to the walls.

Sleeping is also special. Astronauts cannot lie on a bed, so they fall asleep in sleeping bags tied to the wall. Exercise is very important, too. Without gravity, muscles and bones become weaker, so astronauts exercise about two hours every day. Meals are simple, and many of them come in bags. On board, the astronauts see the sun rise and set about sixteen times a day, which makes it hard to follow a normal day and night.
